text:
incident-bot: Pager: high error rate from tenant OxfordLabs in dedicated-vpc-3 during canary. alert_id=ALRT-oxf-9923 link=https://alerts.redwood.internal/ALRT-oxf-9923 count=12/min, 5xx spike, p95 latency 1.9s -> 3.6s. canary window started ~5m ago.

Emily SRE: ack. I'm on it — grabbing logs and canary status.

Raj Oncall: I'm taking primary. Emily, can you confirm if this is traffic-slice sticky routing or global canary?

Mia Runtime: Deploy bot shows a staged canary with traffic-slice=oxf-slice-7 (sticky). Artifact: oxford-service:v2.3.1 -> rollout 5% -> started by @deploy-bot 00:04 ago.

deploy-bot: [DEPLOY] canary rollout: oxford-service:v2.3.1 -> pool=dedicated-vpc-3 slice=oxf-slice-7 canary=5% pinned=false started_by=ci/cd user=jenkins-job-heap

Emily SRE: logs show repeated OOM+KV-cache evictions in the canary pod group. Sample: 
```
[2026-03-15T12:34:10Z] oxford-service ERROR: kv cache overflow, evicting entries, mem=87%
[2026-03-15T12:34:12Z] oxford-service WARN: allocation failure - background flush delayed
[2026-03-15T12:34:13Z] proxy ERROR: upstream 10.2.14.9: connection reset by peer
```

Nora Eng-Infra: sounds like the new build increases memory working set. Did we change quantization flags or tokenizer caching? Mia, any diffs?

Mia Runtime: We switched to per-request KV prefetch in v2.3.1 to reduce latency in cold starts — but that warms the KV cache more aggressively. Missed a memcap tweak for dedicated pools.

Raj Oncall: OK - immediate mitigation options: 1) stop canary rollout (freeze traffic slice), 2) pin artifact back to v2.3.0 for that slice, 3) divert oxford slice to reserved pool running v2.3.0, 4) scale dedicated-vpc-3 temporarily (burst). Thoughts?

Emily SRE: prioritize isolating the tenant. If slice sticky prevents canary from rolling back for that tenant, we should divert slice to reserved pool and pin old artifact. I'll attempt a manual slice divert first.

Jorge CSM: looping in Oxford support. I will tell them we are pausing the canary and isolating their traffic, ETA ~15m. Need a short blurb for them.

OpsScheduler: @Raj Oncall ETA for reserved pool spin-up is ~6m given GPU allocations. Can create a reserved slice if we request now.

Raj Oncall: Emily, run the slice divert command when ready:
```
redwoodctl slice divert --customer oxfordlabs --from dedicated-vpc-3 --to reserved-vpc-pool-9 --slice oxf-slice-7 --force
```

Emily SRE: running the divert now. tailing events.

deploy-bot: [PATCH] pin artifact: setting pinned_artifact=oxford-service:v2.3.0 for slice=oxf-slice-7 by user=Emily SRE

Emily SRE: divert succeeded. Traffic for oxf-slice-7 now routed to reserved-vpc-pool-9 (v2.3.0). Observability: error rate dropping. p95 down from 3.6s -> 1.1s over 90s. :white_check_mark:

Mia Runtime: I'm also initiating an emergency rollback of the canary in the global pool to stop further rollout:
```
redwoodctl rollback --target canary --artifact oxford-service:v2.3.0 --pool dedicated-vpc-3
```

deploy-bot: [ROLLBACK] rollback triggered by Mia Runtime for dedicated-vpc-3 -> target artifact=oxford-service:v2.3.0 status=initiated

Nora Eng-Infra: scaling note: reserved-vpc-pool-9 had headroom for 2x; increased autoscaler min to accommodate slice.

Raj Oncall: customer impact assessment: ~5% of their traffic (the canary slice) experienced 5xxs for ~6 minutes. No data plane corruption detected. We should treat as degraded but contained.

Jorge CSM: sent message to Oxford support channel: "We detected a regression in a canary for your pool and isolated your traffic to a safe pool while we roll back. No data loss expected. Our engineers will follow up with a timeline."

Emily SRE: Confirming rollback completed and all oxf pods on dedicated-vpc-3 are back to v2.3.0. Metrics stabilized: errors ~baseline.

Raj Oncall: handing off to Emily SRE for postmortem. I'll mark the incident as acknowledged and update PagerDuty.

incident-bot: Incident ALRT-oxf-9923 status=resolved severity=medium duration=12m responders=[Raj Oncall, Emily SRE, Mia Runtime, Nora Eng-Infra] runbook=https://runbooks.redwood.internal/dedicated-canary-isolation

Emily SRE: we'll schedule a follow-up to adjust memcap defaults for dedicated pools and add a canary test that exercises aggressive KV prefetch. Action items:
- Mia: reproduce locally and add integration test for KV prefetch + memcap.
- Nora: patch autoscaler memcap for dedicated-vpc-3 pools.
- Jorge: send a short post-incident summary to Oxford.

Jorge CSM: will send post-incident note in 30m.

Mia Runtime: filing an internal ticket: RDW-4567 to track tweak and canary gating.

Emily SRE: closing thread here. Good job team. :thumbsup:
